caseName: Hydrazine propellant tank as primary structure, and the dry skirt beside it
linkedCaseNote: The inherited values below are produced by fluidSystems/codeInterface.py and reused by aerospaceMaterials/codeInterface.py. They are stated here rather than recomputed so the coupling between the three directories is visible in the configuration rather than buried in code.

smallTank._comment: The actual monopropellant tank from the fluidSystems case. Pressure sizes the wall and the resulting R/t is 79.7, the same as at stage scale.
smallTank.jointEfficiencyNote: Fusion welded 2219 girth and longitudinal seams, per fluidSystems Weld

stageTank._comment: The same propellant and the same operating pressure at launch vehicle scale. R/t comes out identical to the small tank, because a pressure-sized wall scales linearly with radius.
stageTank.dryMassAboveNote: Upper stage and payload carried through this barrel section

loadCases._comment: Limit loads. Representative of a small launch vehicle, and the point of the example is which one governs rather than their absolute accuracy.

stiffenedAlternative._comment: An orthogrid barrel of the same radius, as the alternative to a thicker monocoque wall.

mounting._comment: The bolted flange joining the barrel to the thrust structure.

dynamics._comment: A representative small launcher stiffness requirement.

drySkirt._comment: An aft skirt of the same radius carrying the same compression, with no internal pressure to size its wall. R/t is a free choice here and it is chosen thin, which is what makes it a stability problem.
